version.changelog:
- Expanded type assertion best practices, recommending comma-ok and (for Go 1.25+) `reflect.TypeAssert[T]` for reflection.
- Clarified when and how interface nilness can be misleading.
- Updated description and examples for improved clarity, including details on nil behavior for maps, slices, and channels.
- Added reflection-specific type assertion guidance and embedded example.
- Minor corrections to examples (e.g., float comparison), and improved organization for easier reading.
- Version raised to 1.2.1.

llm.summary: This skill provides ordinary Go coding-safety guidance and its disclosed repository-editing permissions fit that purpose.

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently teach defensive Go practices such as nil handling, slice and map copying, numeric bounds checks, resource cleanup, and related eval scenarios.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill requests Read/Edit/Write, search, scoped go/golangci-lint/git commands, and Agent use; these can affect a code repository but are disclosed and aligned with Go code review and repair.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown and JSON files only, declares no install steps, no dependencies, and no executable scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Using Go tools, linters, git, and code edits is proportionate for a Go safety skill; HTTP, token, SQL, and webhook mentions appear only inside coding examples or eval prompts, not as runtime data collection.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No artifact evidence shows background execution, persistence, privilege escalation, credential or session-store access, exfiltration, or automatic destructive behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this for Go projects where you want an agent to review or edit code for safety pitfalls. Because it permits repository edits and scoped Go, linter, and git commands, review proposed changes and commands before applying them in important repositories.
llm.findings:
[SkillSpector clean] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues, and artifact review found no hidden or purpose-mismatched behavior.
[VirusTotal clean] expected: VirusTotal telemetry shows no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this supports the benign result but is not the sole basis for it.
[Static artifact review] expected: The reviewed files are non-executable Markdown/JSON guidance and eval content with no install-time or runtime automation.
